chapter: Lucky Roberts, Armstrong and the big-band rivalries
title: Bubber Miley and John Mack's small-cup mouthpiece
summary: He met Bubber Miley and Tricky Sam; he describes the mouthpiece made for Armstrong that raised the trumpet's range and ruined many players' lips.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Bubber Miley? Yeah, sure thing. Bubber Miley and Tricky Sam (PHONETIC) and all these, yeah. (Inaudible) talking about them when they were in town. Because, see, they were always running. They'd be here and they'd be there and they didn't have much time to hang out.
Did Miley have a big sound?

Yeah, well, Miley had a big sound. All geechies have had big sounds because they had them big mouthpieces. See, here's the thing that changed the trumpet, too. There was a gentleman man named Louie Muck -- no, Mr. John Muck. And he made a mouthpiece for Louis Armstrong. And it made a small cup. And that was when Louis Armstrong started hitting those high notes. And then all those people who knew who were playing the trumpet, it made them somewhat obsolete.

So the range of the trumpet had gone up to D and E instead of A and B flat and high C. See, because it something special when a man hit a high C on the trumpet years ago. In the time of New Orleans. But when this mouthpiece came in, (when Muck) made this mouthpiece, Louis had one of those mouthpieces and he played "Chinatown" and when he played "Chinatown" and hit that high F, that was it.

And he used to have his handkerchief, wiping his face and things, and all the youngsters had handkerchiefs and salve, special salve, tried to talk like Louis Armstrong. Oh, it was (haircut) like Louis Armstrong, and everything. And a lot of them, see, they couldn't adapt to it and destroyed them, destroyed the muscles because they were blowing against themselves and it destroyed all the muscles.
Yeah, it destroyed all of them. And some of the fellows that didn't know technique on the trumpet, they just started blowing and he just tore up the muscles before they were even developed.
